### Principles of complex systems helpers
[This repository](https://github.com/amafehr/pocs_helpers) (in development)
codes helpers for the purpose of making principled complexity methods
quickly accessible for learning or applying. Examples include working with text, understanding your data,
running a linear regression, or calculating and visualizing rank of types in a system.

### Statistical laws in conversations
I analyzed linguistic scaling in conversational texts (naturalistic
and fictional).
<!--(https://gitlab.com/amafehr/convo_scaling)-->
[Results](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.18072)
demonstrate Zipf's and Heaps' laws
in different conversational mediums with differences by parts of speech.

### py-allotax
Working with the creators of the allotaxonometer,
we implemented a python wrapper and interface around javascript implementation to
compare 2 systems' rankings of types. The
[Python py-allotax](https://github.com/compstorylab/py-allotax)
(published on PyPi) allows users to make allotaxonometric
comparisons and plots programmatically. We describe the
allotaxonometric tool ecosystem in
[our paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21808).


### Reddit as network data
I explored modeling
[Reddit posts as conversations and network data](https://github.com/amafehr/stat-6990-reddit-network).
I found that positive replies yields further discussion.
Further, higher user activity can contribute to
their rank rather than needing to be an influential user with high comment
scores across Reddit.

### Linguistic coordination
I assessed the representativeness of
the CANDOR dataset to the U.S. population and analyzed the
linguistic coordination of conversations
<!--(https://gitlab.com/amafehr/linguistic_coord)-->
in CANDOR---how much speakers tailor their linguistic style in responses to the speaker,
confirming this effect in stranger conversations.
